content: 1. Double the dose of larotrectinib when co-administered with a CYP3A4 inducer. Resume the prior dose of larotrectinib after the CYP3A4 inducer has been discontinued for 3-5 half-lives. 2. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of lefamulin by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Monitor for reduced efficacy if co-administration is necessary. 3. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of lemborexant via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 4. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of lenacapavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with moderate CYP3A4 inducers unless the benefits outweigh the risks. 5. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of leniolisib through CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 6. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of letermovir by affecting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Co-administration with P-gp inducers is not recommended. 7. Co-administration of levetiracetam and phenobarbital increases sedation. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Limit use to patients without adequate alternative treatment options. 8. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of lomitapide via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 9. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of lovastatin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 10. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of lumateperone through CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 11. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of lurbinectedin via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 12. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of macimorelin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers may lead to false-positive test results. Discontinue the inducer and allow sufficient washout time before testing. 13. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of macitentan via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. 14. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of mavorixafor through CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 15. Phenobarbital reduces mestranol levels by increasing its metabolism, potentially leading to contraceptive failure. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 16. Co-administration of methohexital and phenobarbital increases sedation. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Limit use to patients without adequate alternative treatment options. 17. Phenobarbital increases the toxicity of methoxyflurane by enhancing its metabolism to nephrotoxic compounds. This combination is contraindicated. 18. Co-administration of methylene blue and belladonna alkaloids increases serotonin levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is necessary, monitor for serotonergic or opioid-related toxicities. 19. Phenobarbital and intranasal metoclopramide enhance each other's effects. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid intranasal metoclopramide or interacting drugs depending on their importance to the patient. 20. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of midostaurin via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Strong CYP3A4 inducers may significantly reduce midostaurin concentrations, leading to decreased efficacy. 21. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of modafinil by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 22. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of naldemedine via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. 23. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of neratinib through CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers. 24. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration in patients chronically using strong CYP3A4 inducers. 25. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of nintedanib by affecting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Avoid co-administration, especially with P-gp inducers that are also CYP3A4 inducers. 26. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of nirogacestat via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 27. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration unless the benefits outweigh the risks. Hormonal contraceptives may not be reliable during co-administration, and backup contraception is recommended. 28. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate and norethindrone transdermal via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration unless the benefits outweigh the risks. Hormonal contraceptives may not be reliable, and backup contraception is advised. 29. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of norgestrel by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially leading to contraceptive failure. Advise patients to use alternative or backup contraception during co-administration and for 28 days after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inducer. 30. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of olanzapine/samidorphan via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Strong CYP3A4 inducers decrease olanzapine and samidorphan levels by approximately 50% and 75%, respectively. 31. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of olaparib through CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. 32. Co-administration of oliceridine and phenobarbital increases sedation. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Limit use to patients without adequate alternative treatment options. 33. Co-administration of phenobarbital and intranasal olopatadine increases the risk of CNS depression, leading to additive psychomotor impairment. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 34. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of olutasidenib via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Strong or moderate CYP3A inducers decrease olutasidenib plasma concentrations and efficacy. 35. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of omaveloxolone through CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 36. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of omeprazole via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 37. Co-administration of opicapone and phenobarbital increases sedation. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Limit use to patients without adequate alternative treatment options. 38. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of osimertinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A inducers. 39. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of ozanimod by affecting CYP2C8 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP2C8 inducers, as this may decrease the efficacy of ozanimod. 40. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of palbociclib via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Strong CYP3A inducers reduce palbociclib plasma exposure by approximately 85%. 41. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of palovarotene by inducing CYP2E1 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 42. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of pemigatinib via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 43. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of perampanel by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 44. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of pexidartinib via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 45. Phenobarbital reduces the effects of phenindione by increasing its metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 46. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of pirtobrutinib via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 47. Phenobarbital reduces the levels of pomalidomide by inducing CYP3A4 and CYP1A2 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 48. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of ponatinib via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration unless the benefits outweigh the risks. Monitor for reduced efficacy. 49. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of pralsetinib via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, double the pralsetinib dose starting on Day 7 of co-administration. Resume the previous dose 14 days after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inducer. 50. Co-administration of pramlintide and belladonna alkaloids results in synergistic inhibition of gastrointestinal motility. This combination is contraindicated. 51. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of pretomanid via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers. 52. Phenobarbital reduces the effects of protamine by increasing its metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 53. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of quizartinib via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 54. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of ranolazine via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 55. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of repotrectinib via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Repotrectinib is a CYP3A4 inducer and may reduce the efficacy of CYP3A substrates. 56. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of ribociclib via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A inducers. 57. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of rimegepant via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 58. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of ripretinib via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 59. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of ritlecitinib via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A inducers, as this may reduce efficacy. 60. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of rivaroxaban via CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 61. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of rolapitant via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Long-term co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers may significantly reduce rolapitant efficacy. 62. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of romidepsin via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 63. Co-administration of ropeginterferon alfa-2b and phenobarbital may result in additive neuropsychiatric side effects. Avoid use and monitor for excessive CNS toxicity. 64. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of selinexor via an unspecified mechanism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Selinexor may cause neurological toxicities, and co-administration with medications causing dizziness or confusion should be avoided. 65. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of selpercatinib via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 66. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of selumetinib via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 67. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of sildenafil via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug.
